newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Buenos Aires gets $1.1bln windfall from power sale. [CORRECTED 21:11 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Buenos Aires gets $1.1bln windfall from power sale. [CORRECTED 21:11 GMT]

text.p: Buenos Aires Province's sale of the distribution business of its electricity firm ESEBA for $1.1 billion raised more than the government had expected, the company's President Jose Romero said Tuesday.
"Technicians had initially forecast we would get $700 million for the distribution area," Romero told Reuters in an interview. "We are more than happy."
Two groups won a 95-year concession for the distribution business. The firm was split into three distribution units, two generation units and one transport unit for privatization.

AESEBA-CEA, formed by U.S. AES Corp and New Jersey based CEA (Community Energy Alternatives), an independent power producer owned by Public Service Enterprise Group, offered $565 million for Eden, serving the northern part of the province, and Edes, serving the southern part.

Inversora Electrica de Buenos Aires, formed by United Utilities Plc -- a U.K. electricity firm --, the local unit of Italian gas firm Camuzzi, Argentine cement producer Loma Negra and also local Citicorp Holdings SA offered $404 million (corrects amount) for Edea, serving the Atlantic coastline.
ESEBA will absorb $130 million in debts. Ten percent of ESEBA will remain in the hands of its employees.
"We believe the price offered obeys not so much to what (ESEBA) is today but is rather a bet for its future growth," Romero said.
He added that the distribution sale will mean a more than 50 percent price cut for major consumers over the next four years. From then on prices will be frozen for 10 years.
On the other hand minor consumers will have to pay an average of eight percent more for their electricty.
Romero said after Monday's tender he was "very confident" about the imminent privatization of ESEBA's remaining units.
Buenos Aires Province government sources had forecast a total price of about $100 million for the two generation units and $130 million for the transport unit.
But Romero said he expected to get a total of about $350 million, which would bring ESEBA's total price to $1.45 billion. (Corrects amount).
More than 20 local or foreign groups had expressed initial interest in ESEBA.
Camuzzi and Central Costanera, one of the country's two biggest thermoelectric generating companies, are the two biddders for the generation sector. The winner will be announced April 28.
Central Costanera is 51 percent owned by Chile's ENDESA, controlled in turn by Chile's ENERSIS SA.
The deadline to bid for the transport unit is June 30 and the winner will be announced July 18.
ESEBA has a staff of 4,500 that will be cut to 3,000. The 1,500 people made redundant will be transferred to other public-sector jobs in the province or offered early retirement.
ESEBA has annual revenues of about $700 million. It reverted 1995's $50 million loss to make a $200,000 profit last year. The company serves 1,4 million people.
The provincial government has said all the proceeds from ESEBA's sale will go back to the people through public works.
((--Buenos Aires Newsroom, 541 318-0650--))
